source.title: Flat-LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation over a Flat Loss Landscape
source.authors: Tao Li; Zheng-Bao He; Yu-Jun Li; Yasheng Wang; Li-Feng Shang; Xiao-Lin Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; some extracted table/figure text is garbled, but relevant results are described in the text.
record.tranche_reason: It compares training/test generalization gaps and loss-landscape flatness for Flat-LoRA versus LoRA, using a different intervention and measure from the magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, or removal of memorized examples. Its own results on generalization gap and flatness bear conceptually on V7. Hyperparameter choices and cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to design Flat-LoRA and evaluates its performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation-tolerance measure or its ranking of generalization gaps: its subjects are pretrained transformers, and its flatness evidence consists of random filter-normalized loss slices. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' interpretation: Flat-LoRA improves in-domain and out-of-domain performance by pursuing flatter full-weight minima. Appendix A reports slightly higher training loss and smaller accuracy gaps. These comparisons do not independently establish that flatness causes the improvements or validate V7's generalization measure.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes pretrained models with LoRA plus Bayesian expected loss under filter-wise random weight perturbations; compares with LoRA, rather than testing the original magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that LoRA rank changes performance and loss-landscape sharpness, and that perturbation strength σ changes results; neither is a direct test of V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Flat-LoRA has smaller training–test accuracy gaps than LoRA on CIFAR-100 and MRPC, despite slightly higher training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random weight perturbation during low-rank fine-tuning can reduce generalization gaps in pretrained vision and language transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100, Flat-LoRA has flatter full-weight loss slices than LoRA at ranks 1 and 16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flat-LoRA produces flatter random filter-normalized loss slices than standard LoRA in fine-tuned CLIP ViT-B/32.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267 (2025)
record.problems: Generalization-gap and loss-landscape comparisons are presented as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. The study compares two methods and does not establish that the measured flatness independently tracks gaps across a range of networks.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing held-out performance under natural and random labels.
Network width beyond zero training error; varying LoRA rank does not establish this condition.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance tracking accuracy gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, including comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All corrected states concern whether the rows establish a claim version; they do not deny the reported gap reductions or flatter loss slices. No numerical gap or flatness values can be recovered from the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Widening beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, underfitting regimes, and removal of dropout/weight decay.
The study does not compare the magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance measure against norm- and margin-based measures, nor rank multiple networks by that measure.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
